## What this notebook shows

`viyar` registers a knitr chunk engine named `sas` when the package
loads (as long as `knitr` is installed) -- this replaces knitr's own
built-in `sas` engine (which shells out to a local SAS installation),
so a `{sas}` chunk always submits to Viya once `viyar` is loaded. Any
`{sas}` block in a Quarto document is then submitted to a Viya compute
session you've already started -- the engine never starts or ends a
session itself, matching how R chunks share one implicit R process
throughout a document.

## Setup

Start the session exactly as you would for any other `viyar` workflow --
see `viyar-workflow-demo.qmd` for the full authentication walkthrough
(Workbench managed OAuth vs. `viya_login()` for local desktop R/Positron
Desktop). Nothing about authentication changes for the `{sas}` engine.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| eval: false

library(viyar)
h <- viya_session()
```

## A basic `{sas}` chunk

By default, `viya.output` is `"html"` -- your SAS code's own `ods html5`
output (opened with no `file=`, per `viya_submit()`'s existing
convention) is rendered directly into the document, with no log shown.
This is deliberately a clean-report default, not a debugging default.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| eval: false;

ods html5;
proc means data=sashelp.class;
run;
ods html5 close;
```

## Showing the log or the traditional listing instead

Set `viya.output` to any combination of `"log"`, `"listing"`, `"html"`.
`viya.output: "listing"` is also the documented alternative for
non-HTML Quarto targets (PDF/Typst/docx), where raw ODS HTML can't
render.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| viya.output: ["log", "listing"];
*| eval: false;

ods listing;
proc print data=sashelp.class(obs=5);
run;
ods listing close;
```

## Hiding the SAS source

Standard knitr `echo` applies -- set it to `false` to hide the
submitted code and show only the requested output.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| echo: false;
*| eval: false;

proc means data=sashelp.class;
run;
```

## A chunk where a non-`"completed"` state is expected

By default, any job state other than `"completed"` stops the render
(fail-fast) -- appropriate for a submission pipeline, where an
unnoticed downstream error is worse than a stopped build. Set
`viya.error: true` to suppress that for a specific chunk instead.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| viya.error: true;
*| eval: false;

%put NOTE: this chunk demonstrates viya.error, not a real failure;
```

## Mixing R and SAS data in one document

`{sas}` chunks share the document's R environment the same way they
share `h`: name an R data.frame in `sas.input` and it's written to SAS
(via [viya_write()]) before the chunk's own code runs; name a SAS
dataset in `sas.output_data` and it's read back (via [viya_read()])
into an R variable named by `sas.output_var` right after the code
finishes -- so a *later* `{r}` chunk can reference it by name, exactly
like a later `{sas}` chunk already can with `session: h`. Both options
take one or more values.

```{r}
#| label: mtcars-setup
#| eval: false

mtcars_r <- mtcars
```

By default `sas.input` lands in `WORK.<name>` (matching [viya_write()]'s
own default), and `sas.output_var` defaults to each table's own name --
give it a `"libref.name"` spec instead to land somewhere else, e.g.
`sas.input: "mylib.mtcars_r"` writes to `MYLIB.MTCARS_R`.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| sas.input: mtcars_r;
*| sas.output_data: "work.mtcars_heavy";
*| sas.output_var: mtcars_heavy;
*| echo: false;
*| eval: false;

data work.mtcars_heavy;
  set work.mtcars_r;
  where wt > 3;
run;
```

```{r}
#| label: mtcars-back-in-r
#| eval: false

nrow(mtcars_heavy)
```

Multiple inputs/outputs are just longer vectors -- `sas.output_var`, if
given at all, must have exactly as many names as `sas.output_data` has
tables (matched by position); errors rather than silently mismatching or
dropping extras otherwise.

```{sas}
*| session: h;
*| sas.output_data: ["work.mtcars_heavy", "work.mtcars_light"];
*| sas.output_var: ["heavy_r", "light_r"];
*| echo: false;
*| eval: false;

data work.mtcars_heavy work.mtcars_light;
  set work.mtcars_r;
  if wt > 3 then output work.mtcars_heavy;
  else output work.mtcars_light;
run;
```

The pull is skipped entirely (nothing assigned, for any of the tables in
a multi-output pull) if the chunk's job doesn't reach a `"completed"`
state -- including when `viya.error: true` suppresses the fail-fast
throw for an intentionally-failing chunk, since the named output
dataset(s) were likely never created. `viya_read()`'s own `max_rows`
safety cap (100000 rows, a client-side guard against pulling an entire
CAS-sized table into memory, not a REST limit) still applies to every
table in the pull; override it per chunk with `sas.output_max_rows` if
you know the result is larger and safe to pull in full.

## Chunk option reference

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `session` | *(required)* | R symbol naming the `viyar` handle, e.g. `h` |
| `viya.output` | `"html"` | one or more of `"log"`, `"listing"`, `"html"` |
| `viya.error` | `false` | suppress the fail-fast throw for this chunk |
| `echo` | `true` | show the submitted SAS source (standard knitr option) |
| `viya.poll_s` | `1` | polling interval in seconds |
| `viya.timeout_s` | `300` | give up after this many seconds |
| `sas.input` | *(none)* | R data.frame name(s), each a bare name (-> `WORK.<name>`) or `"libref.name"` |
| `sas.output_data` | *(none)* | SAS `"libref.table"` name(s) (libref defaults to `work`) to read back after the code runs |
| `sas.output_var` | each table's own name | R variable name(s) for the pulled data.frame(s), matched to `sas.output_data` by position |
| `sas.output_max_rows` | `100000` | override `viya_read()`'s row cap for this pull (applies to every table pulled) |

## Clean up

```{r}
#| label: cleanup
#| eval: false

viya_end(h)
```
